h1.label: nc1
h1.why: the link count read from FileStandardInfo is replaced by 1, so a file with another hard link is counted as freed (worker nc1 flipped the links <= 1 comparison instead)

h1.label: nc2
h1.why: the private key for a name that is not valid UTF-16 becomes lossy, so two different unpaired names collide (worker nc2 dropped the failure count instead)

h1.label: nc3
h1.why: the snapshot walk stops descending below 1024 levels, so the deep part of the tree is never planned (worker nc3 capped the delete stack instead)

h2.label: nc1
h2.why: a panic inside the clean thread leaves clean_progress as a failed run instead of the idle object (worker nc1 set busy before the prep guard instead)

h2.label: nc2
h2.why: a completed scan whose record write failed is still treated as written, so last stays on it (worker nc2 deleted the rollback lines instead)

h2.label: nc3
h2.why: the text-form check is turned around (known folder contains the choice), so a known folder under the choice is only found in canonical form and a junction hides it (worker nc3 kept only the canonical form; the first controller try, || to &&, was caught first by the older SERVICE_CANONICAL_ROOT)

h3.label: nc1
h3.why: take leaks one reference, so the service is never released (worker nc1 left the backend in the slot instead)

h3.label: nc2
h3.why: close waits one poll instead of until the clean has stopped (worker nc2 skipped clean_stop instead)

h3.label: nc3
h3.why: the production service config inverts the switch (worker nc3 turned the constant off instead)

h4.label: nc1
h4.old: const inScope = () => version === routeVersion && origin === location.hash;
h4.why: every command result counts as in scope, so a late clean_prepare opens the dialog on the new page (worker nc1 removed the prepare check instead)

h4.label: nc2
h4.why: the reconnect pass never re-reads the current page (worker nc2 removed the loadRoute call instead)

h4.label: nc3
h4.why: leaving the page keeps the stop-failure line, so it shows again on return (worker nc3 never set the flag instead)

h5.label: nc1
h5.why: plan resolution caps a marker depth at 8, so the Rust build-directory target loses depth 12 (worker nc1 changed the marker decode in rules.rs instead; the gate refuses a rule-data-only change)
